subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or a documented decision that current coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: The bug is real enough to keep open, but choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and security, so automation should not pick the final product policy while a linked PR is already under review.

options.title: Narrow and review linked native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after fixing conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress/size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to the broader native exclude-pattern tracker.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point users to plugin/workaround options such as KeepMyClaw only if maintainers explicitly decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review linked native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after fixing conflicts, proof, protected-path semantics, and external-asset behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the most recent current-main routing signal on the touched backup CLI/docs files, while the original and recent backup contributors remain important review context.
